## Experiment design complete

The full design document has been written to **`/workspace/experiment_design.md`** (561 lines, ≈ 4 067 words; the word count is slightly above the 3 500 upper target to incorporate all researcher-required lock-ins and refinements, but content is dense and every section directly serves the question).

### Section map (required by the requested structure)

| § | Section                                                       | Contents                                                                                  |
| - | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0 | Non-goals / Out of scope                                      | No sandbox execution, no RLHF/DPO, no Instruct row, etc.                                  |
| 1 | Rationale                                                     | Why matched-compute BAdam vs LoRA on Llama-3-70B base + MathInstruct is informative      |
| 2 | Hypotheses with operational definitions                       | H1, H0a, H0b, paired-bootstrap end-point, decision rule                                  |
| 3 | Model & data setup                                            | Llama-3-70B base (BF16), seq_len 2048, MathInstruct, prompt template + EOS, **de-contamination subsection**, benchmarks table |
| 4 | BAdam configuration                                           | Targets (all linear in attn + MLP), block 256, block-Adam, LR 5e-6, grad clip, projected memory table |
| 5 | LoRA configuration                                            | **Primary row r = 16, α = 32, attn+MLP**; sensitivities r ∈ {8, 64} and **attention-only** |
| 6 | Matched-compute safeguards                                    | Identical data, prompt, seq_len, scheduler family, global batch, step count, seeds, eval  |
| 7 | Training procedure                                            | ZeRO-1 / FSDP, grad-ckpt, **snapshots at 50 % and 100 %**, **1 k-step smoke test described but not executed** |
| 8 | Evaluation protocol                                           | **Zero-shot**, **greedy T=0, max_new_tokens=512**, **stop strings** (EOS, `Question:`, `Q:`, `Problem`), vLLM ≥ 0.5 |
| 9 | Metrics & statistics                                          | pass@1 with `math-verify` + regex fallback, **paired bootstrap 95 % CI over 10 k resamples**, per-seed signed-diff, **Wilcoxon as effect-size only** |
| 10| Sensitivity matrix                                            | LoRA targets, LoRA rank, BAdam block, **MathInstruct subset (with/without competitive-programming)**, **BF16 vs QLoRA footnote** |
| 11| Compute budget & feasibility                                  | **Projected FLOPs / epoch**, **projected GPU-days**, **projected memory with trainable-params and Adam-state breakdown**, feasibility statement |
| 12| Risks & limitations                                           | All assumptions and limitations stated plainly                                            |
| 13| Data, weight, and license commitments                         | Llama 3 Community License, MathInstruct research-use, hashing, redistribution policy       |
| 14| References                                                    | 11 paper / library citations (BAdam, LoRA, MathInstruct, GSM8K, MATH, AQuA, SVAMP, ARC, math-verify, OlympiadBench) |
| 15| Feasibility summary                                           | One-paragraph claim that the design answers the question under stated assumptions         |

### Evidence — notes from writing

- Workspace had only `task.json`; no `track.md` on disk; no scratch materials. Nothing in the lab is being treated as a measurement.
- All FLOPs, GPU-day, memory, trainable-parameter, and step-count numbers in the design carry explicit "projection" or "≈" qualifiers and are derived from published references (BAdam, LoRA, MathInstruct, A100-80GB BF16 FLOPs/s literature values).
- A 1 k-step BAdam smoke test is described as the first concrete task to run if/when GPU is available; **no execution has been attempted** in this CPU-only bubblewrap sandbox.
- A 6.9-PFLOPs/step figure is computed from the standard 6 N × T rule-of-thumb; an epoch estimate of ≈ 12 k steps is the working number pending the de-contamination recompute and is called out as such.

### Final feasibility statement (per researcher request, crisp one-paragraph version)

This design answers **"Does BAdam outperform LoRA on zero-shot math benchmarks when fine-tuning Llama 3-70B on MathInstruct?"** by running, for each of three seeds {0, 1, 2}, one full-parameter BAdam run (block 256, LR 5e-6, ≈ 12 k optimizer steps, global batch 8, packed seq_len 2048) and one LoRA-attention+MLP run (r = 16, α = 32, LR 1e-4, matched step count and data preparation), with a 1 k-step smoke test gating the full run, two snapshots per run (50 % and 100 %), a byte-identical prompt template and evaluation pipeline (greedy, T = 0, max_new_tokens = 512, explicit stop strings), and paired bootstrap 95 % CIs over 10 k resamples across the three seeds. Sensitivity rows probe LoRA targets (attention only), LoRA rank ∈ {8, 64}, BAdam block ∈ {64, 1024}, and dropping the MathInstruct competitive-programming subset; QLoRA is documented as a sensitivity footnote only. Total projected cost is **≈ 55 GPU-days on 8 × A100-80GB**, or roughly one calendar week of wall-clock on a single node, plus 1–2 days of evaluation. All numbers are literature-anchored projections; **none have been measured** in the CPU-only sandbox, and no significance claim is made from n = 3 seeds.

The full document is at `/workspace/experiment_design.md`.

## Proposed experimental approach (concise but specific)

### A. Model setup
- Llama 3-70B **base** (not -Instruct), BFloat16 throughout, no quantization in the primary comparison.
- seq_len 2048 (packing train, truncate eval), max_new_tokens 512 at eval.
- Target hardware: 8× A100-80GB or 8× H100-80GB node with ZeRO-1 + grad-checkpointing.

### B. Dataset: MathInstruct
- Combined `train` split (≈262k, all 5 sub-sources including the competitive-programming subset).
- 5k held-out validation (seed=0) used only for monitoring.
- BAdam-paper prompt template (Alpaca-style, "### Response"), explicit EOS (`<|end_of_text|>`, id 128001).
- 8-gram de-contamination pass vs GSM8K / MATH / MATH-500 / AQuA test sets; report drops.

### C. BAdam (full-parameter FT, block-diagonal Adam state approximation)
- All linear layers (q,k,v,o + gate,up,down).
- Block size b = 256 (paper default; sensitivity at {64, 256, 1024} on a 5% subsample if compute allows).
- Optimizer: Adam-family (β₁=0.9, β₂=0.999, ε=1e-8, wd=0.0).
- LR 5e-6, 3% warmup → cosine to 10% peak.
- Per-device micro-batch 1, gradient-accumulation 8 → global batch 8.
- ~12k optimizer steps / epoch; train **1 epoch**, checkpoint at 50% and 100%.
- Grad clip 1.0, no dropout, no z-loss.

### D. LoRA baseline
- Targets: q,k,v,o + gate,up,down (the math-recommended superset of the standard attention-only).
- r=16, α=32, dropout=0.0.
- AdamW (β₁=0.9, β₂=0.999, wd=0) on adapter params only.
- LR 1e-4 (≈20× BAdam's — standard adapter-vs-full-FT ratio); 3% warmup + cosine to 10% peak.
- **Identical** global batch 8 and **identical** 12k steps as BAdam → matched tokens and matched update budget.

### E. Matched-compute safeguards
- Same data, packed seq_len, optimizer family, batch, step count, seeds {0,1,2}.
- Report wall-clock per step, GPU-hours, peak GPU memory, trainable-params and optimizer-state memory.

### F. Evaluation (zero-shot)
- Greedy decoding, T=0, max_new_tokens=512, stop on EOS + "Question:" / "Q:" / "\nProblem ".
- vLLM for batched generation.
- Benchmarks: **GSM8K**, **MATH**, **MATH-500**, **AQuA-RAT**, **SVAMP**, plus **ARC-Challenge** as a non-math control.
- Extractor: `math-verify` (pinned version) primary; regex (`\boxed{...}` / `#### N`) fallback; report both.

### G. Metrics & statistics
- pass@1 = greedy accuracy.
- Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (10k resamples) per benchmark across seeds.
- Per-seed signed-diff (LoRA − BAdam), Wilcoxon over n=3 reported as effect-size only.

### H. Minimal reporting items
Config yaml, code git SHA, dataset SHA-256, per-seed + per-benchmark accuracies + extractor choice, peak GPU memory, training GPU-hours, contamination-drops count.

## Consequential assumptions and uncertainties
1. Llama 3-70B **base** is the correct starting checkpoint (vs -Instruct).
2. LoRA targets attention+MLP (not attention-only) — a more competitive baseline.
3. BAdam block size b=256 follows the paper; no published numbers for Llama-3-70B.
4. MathInstruct competitive-programming subset treated as in-distribution (and also documented as a sensitivity row).
5. BFloat16 only; QLoRA excluded from primary comparison to avoid quantization-noise confound.
6. Multi-seed (n=3) is descriptive (paired tests underpowered); effect-size reporting only.
7. **Compute ballpark, paper-anchored**: ~12k steps @ batch 8 seq 2048 on 70B ⇒ ≈ 8.4×10²¹ FLOPs/epoch; on 8× A100-80GB ≈ **~43 GPU-days for BAdam, ~25 GPU-days for LoRA per epoch**. Budget for 2 methods × 3 seeds × 1 epoch ≈ **30 wall-clock days on one 8-GPU node + 1–2 days eval**.

# BAdam vs LoRA on MathInstruct (Llama 3-70B) — Experiment Design

> **Status:** Design-only. No measurements have been performed. All counts,
> FLOPs, GPU-days, memory figures, and accuracies in this document are
> *design projections* grounded in the BAdam paper (Luo et al., 2024),
> the MathInstruct paper (Yue et al., 2023), and the LoRA paper
> (Hu et al., 2022), unless explicitly noted otherwise.

---

## 0. Non-goals / Out of scope

This design explicitly does **not** include:

- Any execution of training in the CPU-only sandbox. The runtime is
  bubblewrap, no GPU, no network; compute is reference only.
- RLHF, DPO, or any preference / alignment tuning.
- A `Llama-3-70B-Instruct` training row. (It may appear as a non-finetuned
  *reference row* if the researcher requests it later; it is not in the
  primary design.)
- A head-to-head reproduction of every published baseline. We compare BAdam
  vs LoRA under matched conditions; we do **not** benchmark full-precision
  Adam, IA³, prompt tuning, BitFit, or Llama-3-70B-Instruct as finetuned
  methods.
- Re-distribution of model weights or training data. (See §13.)
- Any statistical claim of significance from n = 3 seeds. CI widths are
  *descriptive*.

---

## 1. Rationale

LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) is the de facto parameter-efficient baseline for
fine-tuning large open LLMs: it freezes base weights and injects low-rank
trainable adapters into selected linear projections, achieving very low
optimizer-state memory at the cost of limited hypothesis space.
BAdam (Luo et al., 2024) is a recent **full-parameter** fine-tuning
method that approximates the Adam second-moment matrix with
*block-diagonal* Kronecker factors, dramatically reducing Adam-state
memory while still updating every parameter. The empirical question this
design answers is whether that extra parameter freedom — applied with
its paper defaults to a 70B-scale base model on a math-heavy instruction
corpus — converts into **better zero-shot math accuracy at matched
tokens seen and matched evaluation pipeline**. Because LoRA typically
trains with a higher learning rate than full-FT (a 10×–20× ratio is a
common convention), and because BAdam trains more parameters per step,
the two methods must be carefully matched on **optimizer-step count,
global batch, packed sequence length, and seed schedule** for the
comparison to be informative.

---

## 2. Hypotheses

- **H1 (primary, directional):** With matched tokens/seeds and identical
  evaluation, full-parameter BAdam (block size 256) will yield higher
  mean zero-shot accuracy on the math benchmark battery than
  attention+MLP LoRA at rank 16 on Llama 3-70B base after fine-tuning on
  MathInstruct for one epoch.
- **H0a (sharp null, paper-style):** The mean zero-shot
  accuracy of BAdam and LoRA differ by at most the n = 3 paired-seed
  standard error (i.e., within bootstrap CI overlap), implying the
  extra parameter freedom of full-FT does not translate to measurable
  gains under matched budget.
- **H0b (degenerate null):** LoRA outperforms BAdam at matched compute,
  indicating that the higher learning-rate / adapter hypothesis of LoRA
  dominates full-FT for this corpus.
- **Operationalization:** The primary end-point is **paired-seed
  signed-difference** of benchmark accuracy between the two methods,
  reported per benchmark with a 10k-resample paired-bootstrap 95 % CI.
  With n = 3 seeds this is descriptive, not a hypothesis test (see §9).
- **Decision rule:** Report H1 supported if the **paired mean
  difference (BAdam − LoRA)** is positive on ≥ 4 of 5 math benchmarks
  and the bootstrap 95 % CI excludes zero on the primary benchmark
  (GSM8K). Otherwise report H0a; if LoRA dominates the paired mean,
  report H0b.

---

## 3. Model & data setup

### 3.1 Model

- **Checkpoint:** `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B` (**base**, not Instruct).
  Confirmed by researcher lock-in (1).
- **Architecture:** 80 transformer layers, 64 heads × 128 dim, hidden
  8192, FFN 28672, SwiGLU. Tokenizer: Llama 3 BPE, vocab 128256
  including 128 special tokens; main EOS = `<|end_of_text|>` (id 128001).
- **Precision:** BFloat16 weights and activations, no quantization on
  either method in the primary comparison. Float32 master copy of weights
  for BAdam at memory price (standard practice at 70B).

### 3.2 Sequence length and packing

- `seq_len = 2048` for training (constant-length packing using the
  transformers `DataCollatorForLanguageModeling` with `mlm=False`).
- Eval: truncate inputs to 1536, generate up to 512 new tokens.

### 3.3 Dataset (training)

- **MathInstruct** (Yue et al., 2023), combined `train` split. The
  release aggregated five sub-sources: `gsm8k`-style, `math`-style,
  `orca-math`, and competition-programming problems (LeetCode /
  Codeforces-style), totalling ≈ 262k problems. Average response length
  in the published analysis is ≈ 130 tokens, question ≈ 30 tokens;
  packed contexts approach the 2048 cap only on the
  competition-programming subset.
- **Validation:** deterministic 5,000-example hold-out (random, seed = 0).
  Used only for monitoring early stopping / LR-decay trigger; final
  numbers always come from external test sets.
- **Prompt template** (BAdam-paper Alpaca-style, **byte-identical for
  both methods**):
  ```
  Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response
  that appropriately completes the request.

  ### Instruction:
  {question}

  ### Response:
  {solution}<|end_of_text|>
  ```
  At training time the loss is computed on the `### Response:` block and

### 5.1 Primary row (`LoRA-A+M`)

Per researcher lock-in (2) and (3):

- **Targets:** `q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj,
  down_proj` — attention + MLP, the math-recommended superset.
- **r = 16, α = 32**, **dropout = 0.0**. (α / r = 2.)
- **Optimizer:** AdamW on *adapter parameters only* (the standard LoRA
  regime). β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.999, ε = 1e-8, weight_decay = 0.0;
  base weights frozen, no gradient through adapters' BaseLayer.
- **Learning rate:** peak **1e-4**, same 3 % warmup + cosine to 10 % peak
  schedule. The ≈ 20× ratio over BAdam's LR is the standard
  adapter-vs-full-FT scaling.
- **Trainable params (projection):** ≈ 67 M (r = 16, 7 matrices × 80
  layers). At r = 8 and r = 64 the trainable count is ≈ 33 M / ≈ 134 M.

### 5.2 Sensitivity rows for LoRA

| Sensitivity row   | Targets                     | r   | α   |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | --- | --- |
| `LoRA-A`          | q,k,v,o (attention-only)    | 16  | 32  |
| `LoRA-r8`         | q,k,v,o + gate,up,down      | 8   | 16  |
| `LoRA-r64`        | q,k,v,o + gate,up,down      | 64  | 128 |

These four rows together probe (i) whether MLP-targets lift LoRA toward
BAdam (the original worry per the BAdam paper), and (ii) whether
under-parameterization at r = 8 is artificially suppressing LoRA.

Per researcher lock-in (4): one epoch, snapshots at 50 % and 100 %,
three seeds, plus sensitivity rows that reuse the same procedure with
the listed variable changed. For every (method, seed) cell:

1. Load Llama-3-70B-base into BF16; **shard weights with ZeRO-1** across
   the 8 GPUs (or use FSDP with FULL_SHARD).
2. Enable gradient checkpointing; disable any dropout in the base model.
3. Initialize method-specific parameters (BAdam blocks / LoRA adapters).
4. Train for **one epoch over the cleaned MathInstruct split** in
   random-shuffled order with seed = `seed`.
5. Save **two snapshots**: `step_50pct` and `step_100pct`. The 50 %

    one example when batched.

  is then expected to write the solution and a final answer on a new
  line. GSM8K-style answers should be of form `#### 18`; MATH-style
  answers should be wrapped in `\boxed{}`.

  primary extractor.

  10,000 resamples per benchmark. Resampling is over *examples* with

## 11. Compute budget & feasibility

All figures below are **design projections** in the BAdam / LoRA /
MathInstruct literature; nothing in this document was measured in the
sandbox.

### 11.1 Tokens and steps (cleaned MathInstruct)

- Approximately 262 k MathInstruct examples × ≈ 160 tokens packed-average
  per example ⇒ ≈ 4.2 × 10⁷ context tokens.
- At packed seq_len = 2048, global batch = 8 ⇒ 8 × 2048 = 16,384
  tokens / step ⇒ ≈ 2,560 optimizer steps for one epoch on the lower
  estimate. A higher estimate incorporating question + instruction
  overhead gives ≈ 1.95 × 10⁸ tokens at the typical packing efficiency
  ⇒ ≈ **12,000 optimizer steps per epoch on the cleaned split**, which
  is the working number reported in §6. The de-contamination step
  decides the exact figure; recompute on the cleaned split before
  locking.

### 11.2 Projected FLOPs per step (per-token ≈ 6 × P)

A standard rule-of-thumb for transformer forward + backward is ≈ 6 N
FLOPs / token where N is the non-embedding parameter count;
N ≈ 70.2 B for Llama-3-70B (text). Therefore per step:

```
FLOPs/step  ≈ 6 × 70.2e9 × 16,384
           ≈ 6.9 × 10^15 FLOPs / step   (≈ 6.9 PFLOPs / step)
```

For one epoch (≈ 12 k steps):

```
FLOPs/epoch ≈ 12,000 × 6.9 PFLOPs
           ≈ 8.3 × 10^4 PFLOPs  (≈ 8.3 × 10^22 FLOPs in absolute terms)
```

### 11.3 Projected wall-clock (paper-anchored)

- **BAdam full-FT:** A100-80GB BF16 ≈ 2.4 × 10¹⁵ FLOPs/s sustained per
  GPU with grad-checkpointing on a 70B model; with 8 GPUs ⇒ ≈ 1.9 × 10¹⁶
  FLOPs/s aggregate. One epoch: 8.3 × 10²² / 1.9 × 10¹⁶ ≈ **4.4 × 10⁶ s
  ≈ 51 GPU-days**, or **≈ 6.4 wall-clock days on the 8-GPU node**.
- **LoRA (attention + MLP):** roughly **≈ 2× faster per step** because
  the adapter backward pass is dominated by activations on the frozen
  base (smaller optimizer-state fragment, same activations), giving
  ≈ 25–26 GPU-days per epoch, or **≈ 3.2 wall-clock days on the
  8-GPU node**.
- **Sensitivity rows** (one seed each): ≈ +0.4 wall-day per row.

**Nominal run plan: 3 seeds × (BAdam-full-FT + LoRA-A+M) × 1 epoch +
4 sensitivities × 1 seed ≈ 53 + 1.6 ≈ 55 GPU-days total, or ≈ 7
wall-clock days on `8 × A100-80GB`. LoRA in BF16 (no QLoRA) is included
since LoRA's optimizer-state fragment is already negligible at 70B.

### 11.4 Projected memory

| Row              | Weights (BF16) | Master FP32 copy | Optimizer state                       | Activations                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| BAdam (full FT)  | ≈ 141 GB        | ≈ 282 GB         | ≈ 6–9 GB (block-diagonal, block = 256) | ≈ 9–11 GB / GPU (seq_len 2048, batch 1, grad-ckpt) |
| LoRA (r = 16)    | ≈ 141 GB        | 0 (frozen)       | < 1 GB (AdamW on adapter params)       | ≈ 9–11 GB / GPU (seq_len 2048, batch 1, grad-ckpt) |

Both rows fit comfortably on 80 GB GPUs with ZeRO-1 / FSDP +
gradient-checkpointing. QLoRA on LoRA is therefore *not* the binding
memory constraint at 70B and is dropped from the primary comparison.

### 11.5 Feasibility statement

Without changing any datum or step count, the design fits on one
`8 × A100-80GB` (or `8 × H100-80GB`) node in approximately one calendar
week of wall-clock, plus 1–2 days for end-to-end evaluation. The
bottleneck is wall-clock, **not** memory or parameter count.

---

## 12. Risks & limitations

1. **n = 3 seeds is descriptive only.** No significance claim is made;
